# Area audit: each league's data is safe

Step 2.108. Area 5 of [LEADS.md](../LEADS.md): "Every league and every person in it, children first. One league never sees another's data, a person sees only what their role allows, private numbers and contact details stay private, and nothing is lost or deleted by accident."

Written 2026-11-17 by the area lead for data safety, from build branch commit `7443bb1`. It changes no code, no test and no plan. The step's line names this file `data-safety.md`; the lead's brief for this run named it `each-leagues-data.md`, and that is the name used.

## How this was done, and what was not checked

- **Read:** the spec this is judged against (T4, T5; R-14 to R-17, R-23 to R-29, S-22, S-24, T-87, T-95, U-9, U-14, A-5, A-6, T-45, T-51, T-52 in `DECISIONS.md`; P6 §7; the legal brief on children); every query under `packages/database/src/queries` and every store method; every migration's policies and owner-run functions; every command in core's registry; every route, page and server action of `apps/web`; the two-league test (`packages/database/src/isolation`) and the role-against-command test (`packages/database/src/stores/role-matrix.test.ts`).
- **Run, not just read:**
  - The two-league test with a query's league filter taken out, **76 times, one query at a time, in a copy outside the repository** (section 1b), and every one of the 172 queries that run SQL once more with all its league filters made always-true by a loader hook (section 1a).
  - The role-against-command test (210 tests pass) and the core T-81 scan (49 pass).
  - **6,754 requests** to the web app on the made-up world (`APP_ENV=local`, 5,434 requests and 64 posted server actions, as 13 kinds of person against 10 kinds of league) and on the seeded made-up database (`LOCAL_DATA=made-up-database`, 1,320 requests as 10 kinds of person). Every answer's status, headers and body were saved and compared, and searched for every made-up person's email, phone and birth date and for the names that must be withheld.
  - The findings marked High were each requested again by hand from a fresh start of the app.
- **Not checked:**
  - **Nothing ran on real PostgreSQL.** PGlite is one session, so no lock, race, pooler or role question can be judged here (section 6).
  - **The made-up database has no hidden league.** Both seed leagues are live and no screen changes a league's state, so every hidden-against-missing comparison comes from the made-up world. On the made-up database Admin → Teams and the fixture import answer 500 to staff (`NotOnTheDatabaseYet`, step 2.93) and the live feed does not exist.
  - **No made-up person is an admin limited to one program** (the made-up world has a program scheduler only, `stand-in-cast.ts:36`). What such an admin is sent was worked from the code and the role-against-command test, which has one.
  - Club admins, coaches and captains can hold no right any command checks (section 2). Exports and photos do not exist.

## The answer, in plain words

**Can the test copy go online safely, as far as this area goes? Yes.** It holds only made-up data. No finding here sends a real person's details (the staff accounts that will sign in to it) to anyone who should not have them. **One league's data reached another in no request and no test.**

- **The fence.** Every one of the 172 queries that touch league data takes its league from the server's context and names it in the statement. The database refuses every other league's rows on every table. In the 6,754 answers, nobody was sent another league's data.
- **Who may do what.** A person's role decides what they may do, inside each command, for all 104 commands.
- **Private details.** No birth date, email or phone reaches any browser.

What must be fixed **before real leagues, and above all children, are put on it**:

1. **A league that is not yet published can be found by anyone** (D-H1, High). It should look exactly like a league that does not exist (U-9). Instead:
   - the "Make this my team" button answers a visitor differently for it, gives away its internal id, and confirms its team names one guess at a time;
   - the scorer's six tracker routes answer "not signed in" or "not allowed" where a missing league gets "not found" (D-M2);
   - a signed-in person's "not found" page streams in a different order (D-M3).
2. **A child recorded by birth date would be shown by full name** (D-H2, High). The code decides "child" by the tick alone and never reads a birth date. Neither the written R-28 nor the lead's change of 2026-11-17 is built. Today no screen records a birth date, so it cannot yet happen by tapping. It will the day a screen or import does. Step 2.93 part 5 is to build it.
3. **One of the three fences is not proved for the public pages, the bin and two other places** (D-M1). With a query's own league filter taken out, the two-league test still passed for 12 queries that then reached league B once B's records were set up directly:
   - six public reads;
   - the bin's list, restore and purge, where the purge deleted B's binned venue for good;
   - postponed games;
   - the schedule draft's insert.

   19 more cases cannot fail. Row-level security kept B out in every run, so nothing leaks today. But the test that should prove the second fence does not.

4. **Public game pages carry each player's fixed person id** (D-M4). Someone holding an earlier copy can name a player, a child included, after their name has been hidden or removed. Record 070 removed this from the statistics pages only.
5. **Staff screens show every player's full name as recorded, a removed child's included.** That covers the scorer's device, which stores them, and the box score sheet. The spec is silent (D-M5). A rule for T4 is proposed below.
6. **Some reads rest on the page alone:**
   - a scorekeeper's `schedule.read` opens every unpublished schedule in core (D-M6);
   - an admin limited to one program is sent the whole league's settings (D-M7).
7. **Things that are lost for good, or never go:**
   - a box score corrected by mistake cannot be put back (D-M8);
   - a "removed" person keeps their birth date and contact details for ever, where T-52 says they lose them (D-M9);
   - nothing empties the bin yet (step 2.91).

## 1. The fence, whole

T4 §2 puts three fences between leagues:

1. **The request.** The server decides the league and the person from the session and the address.
2. **The code.** Every query names its league (T-28).
3. **The database.** Row-level security admits only rows of the league set for the transaction (T-61).

The two-league test (T-65) runs every registered case five ways, as its header says (`isolation-harness.test-helper.ts:1`):

- **control:** in league B's own scope;
- **app:** in league A's scope with both fences;
- **code-only:** as A's owner with row-level security out of the way, so only the query's own filter keeps B out;
- **both-leagues:** an account with roles in both leagues;
- **no-league:** no league set at all.

### 1a. Every query and every store method

The full table is Appendix A: one row per exported function of `packages/database/src/queries` and per store method. Each row gives how the league gets into each statement, the two-league case that holds it, and whether that case could fail with the filter taken out. Counts:

- **The league always comes from the scope**, never from a caller's argument, in all 172 queries that run SQL:
  - in 145 it is in every statement;
  - in 24 some table is reached only through a join or a sub-select on a fenced table;
  - in 3 it goes through a SQL function (`gameHasPlays` and `gameWasDecided` pass `scope.leagueId` to 0016's functions, which run as the caller; `listAccessNames` calls `access_list_names`, which reads the transaction's league, D-L10).
  - **No query lacks the league.**
- **No SQL is built from strings.** Every `sql` template binds its values. There is no `sql.raw`, `sql.lit` or `sql.ref`.
- **Every function has a case or a reviewed reason.** 172 have cases and 32 are excused:
  - 21 shape a row already read;
  - 2 build a select without running it;
  - 2 take a lock or a savepoint;
  - 7 are owner-run lookups that answer before a league is known (`isolation-coverage.test.ts:69`, `:186`; T-221).
- **No store method runs SQL of its own.** 14 store factories are excused as binding queries that have their own cases; `gamesReadStore` and `standingsReadStore` have cases of their own.
- **The database:**
  - every table has row-level security, enabled and forced;
  - every league table's policy is `league_id = current_league_id()`;
  - none is unfenced;
  - the 11 functions that run as the owner (SECURITY DEFINER) are all on the reviewed list in `schema/app-role.test.ts:45`.

  That list is compared with the catalog for schema `public` only (`app-role.test.ts:528`), so one added in `sign_in` or `platform` would not be noticed (D-L10).

- **Could each case fail if its filter were taken out?** Every one of the 172 queries was loaded once more through a Node loader hook that made its league filters always-true at load time (the repository untouched), and its own cases were run through `findIsolationFailures`:
  - **115 cases would fail, as they should;**
  - **28 queries and both read stores cannot fail;**
  - 8 fail only when every one of several filters is taken out;
  - 21 are inserts, whose composite foreign keys refuse a link to another league anyway.

### 1b. The sample: one filter taken out at a time

At least 30 were asked for; 76 were done, across every module, 18 of them writes. Each was done in a copy of the repository outside its folder (`cp -a`, the copy's `.git` and `.env` removed). Each run took out one league filter, ran the subject's group of `isolation-cases.test.ts` (`-t "no case of <name> reaches"`) and every command case that reaches the query, then put the file back and checked it byte for byte (`cmp`). **58 were caught and 18 survived.** A survivor is a query whose filter can go without the test noticing. The test is meant to catch exactly that, so each survivor is a gap in the test, not a leak: in the app, row-level security still keeps B out.

**Why the 18 survived** (D-M1). Every catch came from the code-only run alone. The app run never failed, so with a filter gone row-level security held every time. The loader runs of 1a found the same causes in 19 more cases that cannot fail:

- **Set up through the fence:** `update-game-not-started`, `list-refused-adds`, `change-table-player`, `remove-table-player`.
- **No target named, and A's own row read first:** `find-current-league`, `find-league-audience`, `find-league-time-zone`, `find-league-today`, `leagueDayOf`. `has-recorded-child` always answers yes, because A has a child of its own. The `findLeagueName` case already shows the remedy: it changes A's row first.
- **Dependent on the date:** `list-games-in-window`, `list-games-needing-result`, `list-earlier-rounds`, `list-earlier-round`, and three `games.list_*` commands.
  - SQL's `now()` is the real clock, while B's seeded games start on 2026-12-06.
  - So these cases catch nothing today, and begin to catch around 2026-11-29, 12-07 and 12-13: a test whose strength changes with the calendar.
- **Other public reads:** `list-public-seasons`, `list-season-stat-keys`, `list-season-teams`, and both read stores.
- **Statements no case reaches:**
  - 5 of the 6 branches of `list-binned`'s union;
  - the time zone, team and court sub-selects of `insert-published-games`;
  - the courts reads of `list-season-names` and `list-venues` (unfiltered they would read B's courts, and only a venue match in code hides them);
  - the league reads of `load-schedule` and `update-published-game`.
- **A second filter means one alone is never tested:** `find-table-player`, `list-game-roster`, `list-decided-game-lines`, `list-teams-of-account`, `list-games-by-ids`, `delete-rounds`, and both updates of `set-current-season`.

What T-65 promises ("any success fails the build") holds for fences 1 and 3: every run with both fences, with an account in both leagues, and with no league set passed. For fence 2, the code's own filter, it holds for about four queries in five: the public pages, the bin, postponed games and the draft insert are not proved, and the purge's gap is one that would delete another league's records for good if row-level security ever failed. Proposed step P-3.

### 1c. Every route, and what a hidden league answers

Rule (U-9, U-15, T-229): a league that is hidden from a person must get **exactly** the answer of a league that does not exist. "Hidden" means:

- a draft league, to anyone without an admin area in it;
- a suspended league, to anyone but its owner and admins;
- a league in the bin, to everyone.

Where each route runs the league gate (paths under `apps/web/src/`). "The page gate" is `loadLeaguePage` (`server/load-league-page.ts:81`). It runs `resolveLeagueRequest` once per request, checks the address the proxy wrote (`addressMatchesRoute`) and then `leaguePageOutcome`, whose visibility rule is `mayOpenLeague` (`server/league-gate.ts:134`).

What was compared:

- **Status:** exactly.
- **Headers:** every one, apart from `Date`, `Connection`, `Keep-Alive`, `Transfer-Encoding` and `Content-Length` (it follows the body). `Set-Cookie` was compared by cookie name.
- **Body:** after replacing the short name or id asked for with one placeholder, blanking `"sentAt"`, and blanking React's per-request keys.
- No answer carries a nonce or a request id.
- A missing league gets the same answer whoever asks, on both servers.

The binned league answers exactly as a missing one everywhere. The draft and suspended leagues differ in three places:

**D-H1 (High). "Make this my team" tells anyone that a hidden league exists, gives its id and confirms its teams.**

- **What it does.** The action (`my-team-actions.ts:14`) looks up the league named in the form with `findLeague`. It refuses only one in the bin or a former name (`:22`), reads its seasons' teams through the public stats port, and sets a cookie named by the league's id when the team is one of them (`:39`). Its action id is printed on every league page where the button is.
- **Proof, run again by hand.** As a visitor with no cookie: `POST /harbor-city/teams/rockets`, with the action's field and `league=quiet-pines`, `team=lions`. The answer is `303`, `Location: /quiet-pines/teams/lions` and `Set-Cookie: srl_my_team_01900000-0000-7000-8000-000000000003=lions`. With `league=no-such-league` or `binned-league` it is `303`, `Location: /`, and no cookie.
- **What a visitor learns.** That the draft league exists. Its internal id, which also opens the tracker's routes of D-M2. And, by trying names, which teams it has.
- **`clearMyTeamAction`** (`:58`) has the same flaw, by reading.
- **The spec:** U-9 and T-229 ("not found for everyone else").
- **Why it is High:** it is a fence break on the very rule that keeps a league private until its admin publishes it, reachable by anyone with no account.
- Proposed step P-1.

**D-M2 (Medium). The six tracker routes never run the league gate** (the builder of step 2.153 found it; confirmed).

- **Proof, run again by hand.** `GET /api/v1/leagues/01900000-0000-7000-8000-000000000003/games/01900000-0000-7000-8000-006a00000002/state` answers 401 `{"error":"signed-out"}` to a visitor and 403 `{"error":"not-allowed"}` to a stranger and to the coach. The same request for the suspended league (`…0005`) answers the same. For the binned league (`…0006`) and an id that does not exist (`…00ee`) it is 404 `{"error":"not-found"}` for everyone.
- **The other routes, in the saved answers:** the rosters and reopen GETs give the same pairs. The not-started and session POSTs give 403 `{"status":"refused","code":"not-allowed",…}`. The commands POST gives 400 `invalid-input` for `{}`.
- 196 pairs differ in all.
- **Why only Medium:** a league's id is not public, but D-H1 gives it away.
- Proposed step P-1.

**D-M3 (Medium). For a signed-in person, a hidden league's "not found" page streams its rows in another order than a missing league's.**

- **What is the same:** status and headers, and the set of rows in the page. For visitors and for the binned league the answers are identical.
- **Proof, run again by hand.** `/quiet-pines/teams` and `/quiet-pinez/teams` (a missing name of the same length), as the stranger and as the coach, compared after the one replacement:
  - three runs each give one checksum for the hidden league and another for the missing one;
  - sorting the lines leaves them equal;
  - the metadata row and the 404 row change places.
- **The cause.** For a league that exists, the gate waits for the person's access before it answers "not found" (`league-gate.ts:132`, and `:115` for a former name). For a missing league it does not.
- **The same difference in time.** The extra read (`accessOf`) is the leftover "a hidden league costs one more read" (section 5): it shows in the order of the stream here, and it will show in the time taken on a real database.
- Proposed step P-1.

**What each person was sent, where they may see the league.**

- Searched for: every made-up email, phone and birth date, the seed's contact emails, and the full names of the made-up children and of the player who asked to be removed.
- Found: none of them in any answer to anyone outside the league's staff.
- The only full names were on staff screens (Admin → Teams, a game's admin page, the scorer's rosters), which staff are allowed (section 3 says what the spec leaves open there).
- Public pages show "Jordan I.", "Casey F.".
- The only thing of a hidden league in any answer is D-H1's id.
- The JSON routes' field names were listed level by level for every route and person: none carries a birth date, an email or a phone.

## 2. Roles, whole

**How who may do what is decided.** A command names one permission (`defineCommand`, `packages/core/src/command/define-command.ts`); `hasPermission` (`access/policy.ts:20`) reads the owner and the account's live grants in the command's own transaction (T-75) and asks whether a grant's role holds the permission (`access/roles.ts:96`) at a scope that covers the target (`access/scopes.ts:49`: a league grant covers everything, a program grant only its program). The web app's league gate opens an admin area to anyone holding one of its permissions **at any scope** (`leagues/rules/admin-area-access.ts:11`), so a program-limited role opens every area its permissions name, and from there each page's reads either go through a command (checked again in core) or not (below).

**The role-against-command test** (`packages/database/src/stores/role-matrix.test.ts`) has a row for every one of the 104 commands in core's registry and tries each against 12 actors: owner, admin, an admin limited to one program, registrar, scheduler, editor, scorekeeper, a scheduler limited to one program, a signed-in person with no role, a revoked admin, our staff, a visitor (`:199`). Ran it: 210 tests pass in 64 s. Who should succeed is written out by hand from the spec (`heldBy`, `:377`), not read from core, so a command that checks the wrong permission fails. What it never tries: **club admins, coaches and captains** (its header, `:21`, says their scopes cannot be granted until the teams tables exist; team scopes have been storable since migration 0008, so the reason is out of date); a registrar, editor or scorekeeper limited to one program; a scorekeeper when the league scores "assigned games only"; an archived or suspended league; and what a read **returns** (only allowed or refused). Its own table gives scorekeepers `schedule.read` as core does (`:403`), so it cannot catch D-M6 below.

**Every command**, with the permission it names and where that is checked. "Who may" is the owner and the holders of that permission in `roles.ts` (admin everything but the owner's three; registrar people and registration; scheduler schedule, venues and games; editor the site; scorekeeper `games.score` and `schedule.read`; club admin, coach and captain their own club's or team's rosters), and matches P4 §3 and §4 unless the last column says otherwise. RO: refused in an archived or suspended league (U-9).

The full table, one row per command (its file, the permission it names, where and how that is checked, how many role-against-command rows it has, and where the spec and the code part), is Appendix B. Every command not listed below matches the spec.

**Where the spec and the code disagree** (each also a finding in the list at the end):

- **A scorekeeper can read every season's unpublished schedule draft in core** (D-M6). `roles.ts:124` gives scorekeepers `schedule.read`; with it `get_schedule_draft` (`scheduling/policy.ts:118`) answers for any season, hidden ones included, and `list_venues` and `list_postponed_games` answer too. P4 §4: a scorekeeper sees "a list of their games and nothing else". Only the gate stops it today: the Schedule area needs `schedule.edit` or `schedule.publish` (`admin-area-access.ts:17`), and no scorekeeper screen calls these. This is the leftover "a scorekeeper holds `schedule.read`".
- **`list_postponed_games` filters by neither program nor the season's visibility** (`games/commands/list-postponed-games.ts:37`, `packages/database/src/queries/list-postponed-games.ts:11`): a program-limited role would get every program's postponed games, hidden seasons' included. Nothing in the web app calls it yet (D-L5).
- **A scheduler removes venues and courts but cannot restore them** (`remove-venue.ts:16`, `remove-court.ts:14` need `venues.manage`; `restore-venue.ts:14`, `restore-court.ts:17` need `bin.restore`, admins only), against A-5 "whoever may remove a kind of thing may restore it" (D-L6). And only league-wide owners and admins may list the bin (`list-bin.ts:15`), so a scheduler, registrar or program admin who may restore their own kind of thing cannot see the bin to find it.
- **Not built yet, so not mismatches today:** no command checks a club or team scope, so a club admin, coach or captain can do nothing (stage 4); the roster lock date (S-41) is step 2.138; a scorekeeper reopening a score they typed (S-52) is step 2.177.
- **Unsure, for the lead:** the box score sheet and the tracker's reads are refused in an archived league (`games/policy.ts:50`) though U-9 makes it read-only, not unreadable; a registrar or editor limited to one program can do nothing at all; a program scheduler cannot manage venues; a scorekeeper may list venues (P4 §4 says no, record 019 line 38 says yes, and venues are public on the schedule).

**Checks that exist only in the page or the gate.** Every server action and page under `apps/web/src/features` and `apps/web/src/server` was followed to what it reads:

| Where                                                                    | What it reads or sends                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | The only check                                                                                                                                                                                     | Who gets more than their role                                                                                                                                             |

Core runs no permission check on these reads; saving is refused by core (`leagues/settings/place.ts:65`) | An admin limited to one program is sent the whole league's settings (D-M7; the leftover "the League settings page's read has no check in core")                           |

| A season's team names for the schedule (`database-schedule-admin.ts:65`) | Team names                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Core's `mayListSeason` has already filtered the season                                                                                                                                             | Nobody                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Staff display names in the tracker (`database-tracker.ts:98`)            | A display name                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Used only after a command named the account (S-36)                                                                                                                                                 | Nobody                                                                                                                                                                    |

**What a refusal changes and gives away.** Read for 21 commands across every module: bad input is refused before a transaction opens (`define-command.ts:148`); every other refusal happens inside the command's one transaction and undoes everything it wrote (`:181`, `:203`), including the two that refuse after writing (`record-final-score.ts:47`, `add-adjustment.ts:51`). The one intended exception is a tracker batch, whose accepted taps are kept while refused ones are answered in the reply (`apply-tracker-commands.ts:12`). A target that is not found is checked league-wide, so a program-limited role gets the same `not-allowed` for a missing id, another league's id and another program's id, and a league-wide role gets the same "not found" for a missing id and another league's. The three answers that say a little more (`assign_scorekeeper` says whether an account may score; `reopen_tracked_game` who ended the game; `accept_invitation` the link's state) are told only to someone who already holds a role over the thing or holds the link.

## Appendix A. Every query and every store method

Paths are under `packages/database/src/`. Made from commit `7443bb1` by reading every function and running its own cases with its league filters made always-true (section 1a). The two tables are kept out of the formatter's column padding (`prettier-ignore`), which would make them twenty times their size.

- **Column 3, the league in the statement.**
  - `L=scope` means `where <table>.league_id = scope.leagueId` (for `leagues`: `where id = scope.leagueId`).
  - `ins←scope` means the insert sets `league_id` from `scope.leagueId`.
  - `join(t)` means table `t` is reached only through a join or sub-select on `t.league_id = <a fenced table>.league_id`.
  - Every query below takes its league from the `LeagueScope`. **No query takes a league id from a caller's argument**: every `league_id` comparison and every `leagueId` use outside the scope was searched. The only argument-borne league in this package is the `league` parameter of the four SQL functions of 0016, which the queries fill with `scope.leagueId` or with the row's own `league_id`.
- **Column 4, the two-league case.** It gives the case file (`iso` = `isolation-cases`, `games` = `games-cases`, and so on, all `isolation/*-cases.test-helper.ts`) and the case name, or the excuse from `isolation-coverage.test.ts` (`reachNoLeagueData` or `narrowLookups`).
- **Column 5, could the case fail if the league filter were removed?** Judged by reading, then checked by a **mutation run** (`mut:`). In that run, a Node loader hook rewrote the query file at load time, so the repository was untouched. It replaced every `.where('…league_id' | 'id', '=', scope.leagueId)` with `is not null` and every raw `league_id = ${scope.leagueId}` with an always-true test. Then that function's registered cases ran through `findIsolationFailures` against the real two-league fixture. "mut: caught" means at least one case failed, so the case does test the filter. "mut 1-of-n" lines report removing one filter at a time. The hook and its runs were kept on the audit's machine only (this step writes one file).
  - **"n/a (insert)"**: an insert has no filter to remove. Its league comes from the scope, and the composite foreign keys (every link includes `league_id`, T-40) refuse a row pointing at another league's records anyway.
  - The harness's SQL `now()` is the real clock while the seeded games are in December 2026, so four list queries are **date-dependent** (flagged).
- **Column 6, notes.** "people" means the statement reads or writes `people`. "contact" means it reads or writes contact or sensitive fields. "status by hand" means it writes out the public-season or decided-game state test itself.

## Appendix B. Every command against the roles

Paths are under `packages/core/src/modules/`; inside a cell `m/` is the same folder. "At program" means the check is made at the program of the target's season, and league-wide when the target is not found; "held anywhere" means the permission at any scope passes; RO means refused in an archived or suspended league.
